content.title: Ryanair raises airfares as ‘depressed’ Britons flee UK
content.summary: Ryanair has warned passengers face a double-digit increase in airfares as “depressed” Britons drive a surge in holiday bookings. The airline said ticket prices are set to increase by as much as 9pc in the year through March, more than twice the current rate of inflation. Neil Sorahan, Ryanair’s finance chief, said bookings had climbed to record levels since Christmas as people prioritise spending on holidays even in the face of high living costs and rising taxes.

content.title: Ryanair lifts fare growth forecast on strong early 2026 bookings
content.summary:
STORY: Ryanair on Monday (January 26) boosted its forecast for average fare growth. 

That's after bookings for 2026 got off to a strong start.

And the firm predicted annual after-tax profit would likely jump by a third.

Europe's largest airline by passenger numbers said average fares would be 1 or 2 percentage points higher for the year to March than the 7% annual growth it forecast in November.

The Irish airline said it's "cautiously guiding" after-tax profit to land between $2.5 billion and $2.7 billion.

Ryanair earned an after-tax profit of $136 million in the final three months of 2025.

That was excluding an exceptional $100 million charge related to a fine from the Italian competition authority in December.

Chief Executive Michael O'Leary said in a video statement that he was confident the full fine would be overturned on appeal.

Although he added that it could take a year or two.

Ryanair has been forced to cut capacity growth in recent years due to delays at Boeing.

But it said relations with the U.S. firm are now going well.
